## The founder-emulation items

1. **Who (practitioner `agent`).** YC-C names hotel groups with "call centers and central reservation departments";
   YC-L's video features front-desk staff at a Munich hotel. *My choice:* the reservation agent, central office or
   front desk, who sees the missed-call list. Segment: hotel groups in Germany with a central office or call center.
2. **When (circumstance, occasion, window).** YC-L's "After hours. During peak hours. On holidays." *My choice:* the
   occasion "reservation shift", window the last 7 days (calls come in on every shift; spec 120's "every shift" -> 7
   DAYS), Frequency 5 to 7 days out of 7.
3. **Who pays (decision-maker `director`, Buyer and payer, Purchase friction).** TERMS addresses the hotel group;
   YC-L asks to "book a 10-minute call if you lead a hotel group". *My choice:* the revenue or reservations director
   decides, the hotel's owner has to agree. Purchase friction tests "A data protection review of guest calls" (German
   hotels handle guests' card and personal data on the call); my choice, no source names it.
4. **Mechanism.** YC-C: missed calls forwarded to Codyco, the AI answers, bookings appear in the PMS. Compatibility
   tests call forwarding (the mechanism needs it); Adoption friction tests letting the AI answer in the hotel's voice.
5. **Cost, price, ability.** As in the table. Reading `budget` by the engine (a percent of calls against euros).
6. **Commitment.** TERMS and YC-L: the paid, money-back pilot at one location. The step carries its number ("pay
   €3,000 for a money-back pilot at one hotel"), the gap-8 check.

## The respondents

No first-person account by a German reservation agent or revenue director was found in public (no HN thread; the
site's quotes are curated testimonials). **Every person is the author's invention**, no real person's name is used,
and each is built on the public facts named here.

Reservation agents (Parts 1 and 2):
- Lena Hoffmann: a trade-fair Saturday in a Munich central office; built on YC-L ("During peak hours") and the Munich
  hotel YC-L features.
- Murat Yilmaz: a check-in rush at the desk; YC-L's "peak hours".
- Chiara Russo: a group whose call center already answers after hours (YC-C: "Even with call centers..."); her pain is
  group emails, so Importance and Current solution go against the founder.
- Jonas Weber: alone on a Sunday desk; YC-L's "On holidays" / after hours.
- Aylin Demir: an old phone system that cannot forward (Compatibility only_with_help); the author's.
- Tobias Brandl: the sceptic who will not hand guests to an AI (Relative advantage negative, Adoption no); the author's.
- Elif Kaya: weekend abandoned calls seen on Monday; YC-L's "After hours".
- Daniel Okonkwo: rates pushed wrong to agencies matter more (Importance against); the author's.
- Mehmet Arslan: a vague story, GUESSED. Katarina Novak: a story chip, GUESSED.
- Florian Gruber, Nadia Haddad: gate No (no unanswered booking call in the 7 days).

Revenue directors (COMMERCIAL_B2B link, Part 3): Stefanie Wagner (6%), Andreas Keller (4%, below the founder's 5%),
Roberto Bianchi (8%), Ingrid Lindholm (2%, a call center covers after hours), Karim Benali (does not know his rate;
YC-L's "Free AI Strategy Workshop" and SITE's free test number as his ask), Petra Vogel (5%), Hannes Moser (nothing,
would not pay), Joanna Wiśniewska (10% at resort hotels in high season). The value boxes are percents of the calls, in
the founder's unit and period; the price picks are two codes, the pilot's rung and the licence's rung, each placed
against the founder's €3,000 and €1,000.

## Status today

Same idea (SITE, 2026-10-22): "Turn missed hotel calls into paid bookings.", widened to payments, invoices and
handovers; "Running at 15+ hotel groups" (the launch said 7); "€10k+ bookings written directly into the PMS". **No
public price today** (SITE and /faq show none); the €3,000 pilot terms remain the only priced source.

## Open (what could not be sourced, and the workarounds)

- **The licence amount** was never public. €1,000 to €1,500 per hotel a month is the operator's reading of the pilot's
  monthly rate (above). Treat the plan step's reading as a reading of that derivation.
- **Dollars or euros.** YC-L says "$5,000", YC-C "€5,000" for the same hotel; the pilot fee is in euros and the company
  is in Munich, so the entry is in euros. The market is DE, and the golden corpus's rule U (US only) is a note.
- **The "> 8 hotels" / "10 hotels" roll-out threshold** in TERMS and YC-L disagree; the entry does not use it.
- **Job titles.** Neither the agent nor the director is named in public; both are my choices (items 1 and 3).
- **The 5% is the founders' claim** for "the best" offices; no independent figure was sought.
- **UPFRONT_THEN has no "credited" or "money-back" flag**; the fee is a plain up-front amount (header).

screens.why3: I sit in these sales calls with revenue directors and know what holds them up, so I can answer from what I see.
screens.why4: 'A trial at one hotel first' is my own pilot offer, not a brake, and it overlaps with 'a check that bookings land in our PMS', which is what the pilot proves, while the owner's sign-off and the works council or IT review of call forwarding are missing.
screens.why5: The belief and the bar keep my data-protection pick word for word, and the options don't leak Codyco or the AI to the director.
screens.instead: What slowed your last purchase of a guest-facing system most? A data protection review of guest calls / The hotel owner's sign-off / A works council or IT review of the phone setup / Proof that bookings land in our PMS / Nothing slowed it

screens.why1: The last commercial question (6 of 6) asks for the paid pilot I ask hotel groups for, after price, who agrees and what slows a purchase, so it is obviously asked here.
screens.why2: The question and hint are plain, but Keel's belief line, "Most are open to pay", drops who "most" are (the revenue directors) and is ungrammatical, so I read it twice.
screens.why3: The first step I ask of a hotel group is my own offer, the €3,000 money-back pilot at one location, so I answer it from what I do every week.
screens.why4: There are no options here, only a box I type in, and the single escape chip, "Leave this out of the study", fits a founder who has no step to test.
screens.why5: The belief keeps my step word for word, with the €3,000, the money-back and the one hotel; only the crediting on roll-out is left out, and I did not type that here.
screens.instead: Belief: Most revenue directors would pay €3,000 now for a money-back pilot at one hotel.

screens.why1: After I named the first step, Keel shows the belief it will test about that step; it is the last of the six commercial beliefs, so it belongs here.
screens.why2: I understand it, but 'Most are open to pay' is broken English ('open to paying'), and 'Most' does not say most of whom; I have to read it twice to see it means the revenue directors.
screens.why3: The €3,000 money-back pilot at one location is my own offer from the partnership terms, so I can judge this belief from what I know.
screens.why4: This is a card to check; it shows no options, rows, chips or value box.
screens.why5: It keeps my €3,000, money-back and one-hotel pilot; it drops the fee being credited on roll-out, but that does not change the belief.
screens.instead: Most hotel group revenue directors would pay €3,000 for a money-back pilot at one hotel.

screens.why1: After setting the money-back pilot as the first step, a screen that says this pilot is about to be locked and turned into the questions strangers will see belongs right here before sending.
screens.why2: "The pilot" with "Locking freezes your beliefs" is understandable, but "freezes your beliefs" is tool-talk, not how I would say it, and "The pilot" as a heading alone does not say whether it means my €3,000 hotel pilot or Keel's pilot of the study.
screens.why3: It asks me only whether I'm ready to lock what I typed, which I know.
screens.why4: A single "Continue" is fine to move on, but there is no visible way to go back and change a belief before it is frozen, and that is the choice I would want on a locking screen.
screens.why5: "The pilot" is ambiguous next to my own money-back pilot at one hotel, so the screen's meaning drifts a little from what I typed, though nothing leaks to respondents.
screens.instead: Ready to send? Locking keeps your beliefs as they are and writes the questions reservation agents and directors will be asked. [Lock and write the questions] [Go back and change something]

screens.why1: Choosing who runs the interview is the natural last setup step before the study goes out to reservation agents and directors.
screens.why2: "Lock and record the interviewer" and "Keel's credits" are tool words, not mine; I'd need a second read to see that I'm picking the AI voice and paying for it.
screens.why3: It's my own decision as the founder about how my study is run, which I know.
screens.why4: A preselected face with a lock-and-record action works, but the screen doesn't show what the other choice is (me asking, or a plain text form), so the alternative is unclear.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or my hotel roles is changed or leaked here; it's a setup choice about the interviewer.
screens.instead: Who asks your questions? — The AI interviewer, by voice (uses Keel credits) / A written form they fill in by text / I'll ask them myself
